decision: copied research.md and design.md unchanged as the first commit
why: the brief asks the history to show the originals

decision: keep the trail in bench/firmware/decisions.tsv and commit it
why: an unattended run the user reviews later, so the reviewer needs the trail

decision: fetch each release's rootfs tarball instead of unpacking disk images
why: every release and target ships *-rootfs.tar.gz, so no unblob or squashfs is needed and tarfile's data filter is the only parser

decision: aarch64 from armvirt/64 then armsr/armv8, armv7 from armvirt/generic, armvirt/32 then armsr/armv7
why: the VM targets exist for every release and build the same packages as routers of the architecture

decision: label from Makefile and patch list at each tag, fix versions from upstream changelogs and git tag --contains
why: the brief bans version-string labels; memory of fix versions was wrong once (dropbear CVE-2018-15599 is fixed in 2019.77, not 2018.76)

decision: count CVE-2022-0934 and CVE-2020-25681 as absent in stock images
why: stock images ship the dnsmasq variant built with NO_DHCP6 and without DNSSEC; the binary's compile options say no-DHCPv6 no-DNSSEC

decision: match a fix by commit subject as well as ancestry
why: 25.12.5 carries the odhcpd fix as cherry-pick d08dbcc; ancestry alone labelled it vulnerable

decision: cross-check labels against binary strings for Terrapin and dnsmasq compile options
why: prove the labels on the real binaries before building on them

decision: build package-swap variants (dnsmasq-full from the release feed) before any SDK work
why: real shipped binaries give exact labels for the DHCPv6 and DNSSEC advisories with no build and no downloaded code run
result: 6 variants, compile options show DHCPv6 DNSSEC

decision: finding: recore found 0 functions in every OpenWrt binary
why: OpenWrt sstrips every program, which removes the section header table, and recore reads code and symbols only through sections
evidence: recore summary on 40 binaries, readelf: There are no sections in this file

decision: fix it in recore instead of stopping: rebuild section headers from program headers and the dynamic table
why: a contained loader change that only runs when e_shnum is 0, and checkable against truth by deleting the section headers of corpora that have it; without it the benchmark has no recore arm

decision: fixed four mistakes the truth corpora exposed: lld puts .init after .text, GNU hash has no chains when nothing is exported, a NOTE table hid .rodata, the Thumb PLT prefix can be bx pc; b .
why: each showed as a gap between the sectionless copy and the original score
result: copies score as originals on all four corpora

decision: put the fix in its own PR off main (sectionless-elf)
why: out-of-band fix to recore, reviewable without the benchmark

decision: fleet sweep: 3,228 distinct executables and libraries load with no failure; 5,624 kernel modules load with 0 functions
why: the brief asks that recore load and analyze every image binary

decision: fixed .text ending at DT_FINI in musl libc.so, which places .fini mid-code
why: Ghidra comparison showed recore with 225 of libc's ~1,750 functions

decision: left retpoline import calls in 19.07 x86_64 as a finding, not fixed
why: a codegen pattern of one release series; recore sees 3 of dropbear's 152 imports there; fixing it is a separate change to the x86 analysis

decision: Ghidra headless twice over 81 binaries (9 per release-arch), recore summary 5 runs each pinned and all cores, alternated
why: the research lists this measurement as open before quoting any speedup; two Ghidra runs check repeatability
result: Ghidra 487/498 s analysis, 761/779 s wall; recore 1.9 s one core; 257x overall, 265x median

decision: report the ratio as 257x, not the README's 1,000x+
why: Ghidra is fast on small OpenWrt binaries (6 s each, research said 43-84 s for larger busybox); recore's time is analysis (help is 1 ms, busybox 51 ms analysis)

decision: rewrote the claim that Ghidra cannot fit the budget: it fits for single-daemon advisories; speed only counts for library, bundled-copy and unnamed-component advisories
why: measured 9.4 s wall per binary makes 50 daemons about 8 minutes

decision: pilot: 10 images over 3 arches, 3 advisories (Terrapin with a string tell, CVE-2022-0934 compiled out or backported, CVE-2026-5172 code-only with backports)
why: one advisory per pitfall type; 7 of 30 cells are traps for a version scanner

decision: Ghidra arm gets every image's dnsmasq and dropbear pre-analyzed, named imgNN-program, analysis time recorded
why: pyghidra-mcp names programs by file name, so ten dnsmasq files would collide; pre-analysis mirrors bench/agent

decision: haiku recore session: 10 of 30, all Terrapin cells right from strict-KEX strings, all 20 dnsmasq cells undecided after 309 s
why: the agent would not decide without code evidence and quit early

decision: audited the recore session with audit.py and by reading every non-recore command
why: the brief asks for a cheating audit
result: clean: grep only over the package database and saved decompiles

decision: finding: ARM string references mostly missing (used by: none), the same with and without section headers
why: the agent's friction report named it; checked on Debian armhf less (377 of 744 none either way)
evidence: recore-mcp strings on 23.05.6-armv7 dnsmasq: 342 of 400 none
result: open finding, not caused by the loader change

decision: did not build SDK variants (patch dropped, patch added); shipped the natural fleet plus package swaps
why: the SDK is a downloaded toolchain and build scripts, and the constraints say never execute downloads; the brief allows shipping the natural fleet first
result: open: needs a sandbox decision from the user

decision: haiku ghidra session: 2.5 of 30, six Terrapin cells called vulnerable on string absence (one wrong), 24 unresolved, stopped after 196 s
why: same early stop as the recore arm; addresses given as unknown, so evidence scored half
result: both arms far below the version scanner

decision: run a second Haiku session per arm
why: one session per arm cannot tell separation from noise; each costs about 0.2 dollars

decision: opened #22 (design) and #23 (fleet and labels) stacked on it, and #24 (sectionless loader) on main
why: small PRs a reviewer can verify alone; the loader fix stands without the benchmark

decision: moved the budget correction into #22 and rebased the unpushed stack on it
why: a reviewer of the design PR should not see a claim the measurements disproved

decision: second sessions: recore 10 of 30 again, Ghidra 7 of 30 (all ten CVE-2026-5172 cells called fixed, two right by chance)
why: checks whether the first pair's gap was noise

decision: audited all four sessions; one breach: haiku-ghidra-2 read its own oversized MCP result saved under ~/.claude/projects with python3
why: folder rule; the file is the session's own tool output, not labels
result: reported in results.md, cells not voided

decision: cargo test --release --workspace on the measurement branch
why: CI runs the same command

decision: replaced the odhcpd advisory text I first wrote (an out-of-bounds read, no CVE) with NVD's text for CVE-2026-53922, a stack overflow
why: my first text was written before reading the fix commit; the commit names the CVE and NVD published it on 2026-10-12

decision: added .plt to the rebuilt sections, then fixed .plt.sec detection firing on _start's endbr64
why: armv7 dnsmasq showed 0 imports without .plt; the fixture test caught the missing _start at 0x1050
result: 167 imports on armv7 dnsmasq, test green

decision: pyghidra-mcp names programs with a hash suffix (img10-dnsmasq-82115a), not the img10-dnsmasq the prompt says
why: found in the server log after the prompt was written; the agents listed the real names and went on
result: prompt wording to fix in a later round

decision: cross-family review of the trail and docs by opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free: 12 flags
why: show-me-your-work asks for a reviewer of another model family; it read the committed trail and docs, not the session transcript, which holds the user's private instructions

decision: acted on 4: labeller checks dnsmasq compile options against the variant rule; version guard needs version plus dash; audit reads MCP tool arguments; results no longer heads the pilot 'Headroom, plenty'
why: absent rested on package name alone; startswith let 2.8 match 2.80; MCP import_binary paths went unchecked; every F1 sat below the trivial baselines

decision: left 8 flags as already stated limits: no tool separation on hard cells, two sessions per arm, loader heuristics without OpenWrt truth, kernel modules, ARM xrefs, 257x not core-equalized, tiers B and C need SDK builds, earlier rows saying running
why: each is reported in results.md or the PR bodies; the trail is append-only, so later rows give the outcomes
